label: step 1 (second input token) when the first token is in a fixed set of 18 tokens
explanation: Fires only at step t=1 (the second original input), on every L, and only when the first original token is one of a c d e g h i l n o q u v w x y 0 2. It fires on all such sequences and never otherwise: on dev, precision and recall are both 1.0. It never fires when the first token is b f j k m p r s t z 1 3, and never at any other step (including the delimiter and copy phases). Activation is nearly binary (mean 2.0, range about 0.8 to 1.0 of max). The top examples (1.00) all start with q. In the examples checked, starting tokens v, i and l gave the lowest values (about 0.82). That suggests magnitude depends mainly on the first token, but this was not checked systematically. The token at step 1 itself has little effect on whether it fires: every in_tok shows the same rate.

issues: No systematic gap found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.999997, F1 0.999998, mass recall 0.999999 and correlation 0.998. The only miss is a single weak activation (0.24) at a copy-phase step, step 16 of '0 c v c v w z z 0'. That is noise.

The dev profile backs up the factual claims. Every activation is at t=1 (rate 0.602, which is 18/30 of sequences). The feature never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, on dev or test apart from that one test step. The rate is flat across in_tok (0.051 each) and across prev_tok (about 0.092 to 0.093) for the included first tokens.

The magnitude claims check out. Activation is near-binary, with mean 2.005, median 2.013 and max 2.243, and the lowest-quartile examples sit at about 0.81 to 0.84 of max. Activation mass share differs by first token even when counts are nearly equal (w 0.061 vs h 0.049), so magnitude does depend on the first token. The explanation hedges this point, which is appropriate.
Minor wording quibble: 'every L' is true, but the rate per step drops with L only because sequence length grows. Per sequence, the firing rate is constant at 0.6.
